title: Why We Always See the Same Side of the Moon
description: Why the Moon spins exactly once per orbit, called synchronous tidal locking, from NASA and ESA.
narration: Have you ever wondered why the Moon always shows us the same face? The Moon does rotate, but it takes exactly as long to spin once as to circle Earth. As a result, we never see the Moon's far side from Earth. Scientists call this synchronous tidal locking. Over time, the Moon's spin slowed down until one spin took as long as one trip around Earth. Even today, Earth's pull stretches the Moon into a slight football shape. All the large moons in our solar system are locked to their planets this way.
